subject.title: Renderer placeholder leak: `(see attached image)`, `Image reply`, `Audio reply`, `Media reply` leak to human-visible Telegram reply under specific content-classification paths

question: Should implementation wait for a live Telegram boundary trace that identifies where the placeholder first becomes channel-visible text?
rationale: The same literals intentionally serve provider and WebChat transcript contracts, while current source does not connect them to Telegram delivery; choosing a fix boundary without runtime evidence risks changing the wrong subsystem.

options.title: Require boundary trace
options.body: Reproduce the turn with redacted logs for provider output, normalized reply payload, transcript projection, and Telegram request before authorizing code changes.

options.title: Suppress literals globally
options.body: Remove or blank the shared placeholder strings despite uncertainty about their provider and WebChat transcript contracts.

recommendation.title: Require boundary trace
recommendation.body: Reproduce the turn with redacted logs for provider output, normalized reply payload, transcript projection, and Telegram request before authorizing code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest implicated current-main surface is the WebChat media/transcript helper introduced through this contributor's merged work, and the issue timeline already routes attention there.
